items.text: Every aircraft but trail turns its anti-collision light off at REDCON 1. Trail starts the REDCON 1 report in reverse chalk order; when lead reports REDCON 1 the flight is ready. items.label: Loss of visual contact (in-flight link-up and rally points)
items.text: Lost visual: use every digital aid, then call blind on internal. The aircraft you lost gives its heading, airspeed, MSL altitude, and bearing and distance from a common point, and shows trail lighting. You slow 10 knots below its airspeed and climb or descend 200 feet. Once visual, close at no more than 10 knots above it and call closing; trail calls saddled. Not visual: continue as two flights in radio contact and link up on the ground at the next landing zone. Rally points are ACP2 (inbound), RP5 (outbound).

items.label: IIMC
items.text: IIMC: announce it with your chalk and heading, go to instruments, never descend. Base altitude 4,000 ft MSL, adjusted 500 feet for each subsequent chalk; base heading the mountain heading, plus 10 degrees times your chalk number to the clear side; base airspeed 100 KIAS, less 10 knots for subsequent chalks. Contact the controlling agency. Recovery is ________.
